rationale: parse_block scans the complete raw structured unit for mdBook include/playground/rustdoc_include forms, so literal samples do not bypass rejection, and scans fenced body directives to reject nested legacy citations. validate_chapters reads each received chapter original source and compares ordered unit IDs and exact raw unit bodies with the processed chapter before process_configured renders it. This matches the authored scope: alterations within received chapters are checked, while omitted whole chapters and later output processing are explicitly outside the claim. Selected tests cover both Lean- and Rust-backed bodies, literal playground text, legacy nesting, preservation of legacy authoring outside structured units, refusal to prepare invalid evidence, already-expanded includes, injected units, and changed prose. The separately marked actual-mdBook test runs the executable pipeline after links expansion and asserts rejection for two external include contents. I inspected that test and the retained historical execution log but did not execute it. Moving book.rs selections to the captured Renderer.lean fixture does not change these self-contained regression inputs or the production boundary.
limitations: This review compares the documented contract with implementation and regression assertions; it is not a proof of implementation correctness or a claim of test execution.
Conservative source/context snapshots were inspected for the relevant behavior and changes, not as an exhaustive audit of every unrelated declaration or paragraph.
